finalText:
It's a small Node HTTP service, five files, no framework. Here's how a request flows through it.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
A[server.js] -->|checks token| B[auth.js]
A --> C[routes.js]
C -->|reads| D[cache.js]
C -->|writes| E[store.js]
D --> E
```

- **`server.js`** — the front door. Checks every request's token, then hands it off.
- **`auth.js`** — makes and checks bearer tokens, signed with a shared secret.
- **`routes.js`** — three endpoints: get a user, list orders, add an order. Reads go through the cache, writes go straight to the store.
- **`cache.js`** — a small in-memory cache, 256 items, keeps recent reads warm.
- **`store.js`** — the actual data, also in memory. Each record forgets itself 15 minutes after it's last written.

Worth knowing: nothing here is saved to disk. If the process restarts, all users and orders are gone. It's built as a stand-in for a real database, not one yet.
